preamble: Depalatalization (hardening) removes the palatal secondary articulation of [tʲ]. In Late Common Slavic, consonants were phonetically palatalized before front vowels and front jers. East Slavic (Russian) and Polish kept this softening, but South Slavic and Czech hardened word-final /tʲ/ after the loss of the jers and Ukrainian hardened consonants before /e/.

examples.note: Final /tʲ/ arising before the front jer lost its palatalization.
Hard final t, as throughout South Slavic.
Czech hardened the final consonant, contrasting with Polish kość [kɔɕt͡ɕ], which kept it soft.
Ukrainian consonants hardened before /e/, unlike Russian, which keeps [tʲ].

sources: Schenker, A. M. (1995). The Dawn of Slavic: An Introduction to Slavic Philology. Yale University Press.
Shevelov, G. Y. (1979). A Historical Phonology of the Ukrainian Language. Carl Winter.
